# Question: `generator-shortcuts`

> For this generator, name the strongest plausible shortcut or rival rule that
> fits the canonical demonstrations. Give an exact input on which it disagrees
> with the intended rule, how you checked the output, and whether your proposed
> generator emits such cases.

## Answer

The strongest shortcut is **reflect about the geometric center of the grid,
ignoring the color-8 divider position**. It fits all three canonical
demonstrations because each canonical divider is centered: column 3 in width 7,
column 4 in width 9, and column 5 in width 11.

The repaired generator emits this exact easy-band case at seed `0`, sample index
`1` (generator SHA-256
`8ae178585a2dbad22de7f3673e5518cdc376358d57c8b0f093c3011680bb20f6`):

```text
input (5 × 8; full-height divider at column 6)
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 0
0 0 0 0 0 2 8 0
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 0
0 0 0 0 0 2 8 0
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 0
```

The intended divider rule copies column 5 to column 7:

```text
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 4
0 0 0 0 0 2 8 2
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 4
0 0 0 0 0 2 8 2
0 0 0 0 0 4 8 4
```

The grid-center shortcut instead reflects column 5 to column 2 and leaves
column 7 blank:

```text
0 0 4 0 0 4 8 0
0 0 2 0 0 2 8 0
0 0 4 0 0 4 8 0
0 0 2 0 0 2 8 0
0 0 4 0 0 4 8 0
```

I checked the case three ways: `self_check` accepts the input; the independent
Python rival disagrees at ten cells; and `arcpuzzles apply` executed the selected
Racket authority (`RULE_HASH 55bc14a48684`) and exactly matched the intended
output. The source-bound data and authority receipt are:

- `checks/question/grid-center-witness.json`
- `checks/question/grid-center-witness-apply.json`

Yes, the proposed generator emits such cases deliberately. Every odd schedule
slot is off-center. In the 600-draw semantic census, the off-center witness fired
294 times; the exhaustive eight-slot census and the 300-lesson random census
both found zero ordered or rotated lessons in which this declared rival survived.
